title: Safe Deposit Boxes: Late Rent, the Grace Period and Past Due Status
content:
When a year's rent on one of the bank's Safe Deposit Boxes goes unpaid, a grace period runs from the rent due date. This page states when that period ends, what a lessee is charged once it has ended, and what the rental's status means for getting into the vault.

## Terms by box size

| Box size | Late fee per rental year (USD) | Grace period | Vault access while past due or drill pending |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3x5 Safe Deposit Box | 15.00 | 30 calendar days | Refused |
| 3x10 Safe Deposit Box | 15.00 | 30 calendar days | Refused |
| 5x10 Safe Deposit Box | 20.00 | 30 calendar days | Refused |
| 10x10 Safe Deposit Box | 25.00 | 30 calendar days | Refused |
| 10x15 Safe Deposit Box | 25.00 | 30 calendar days | Refused |
| 10x20 Safe Deposit Box | 30.00 | 30 calendar days | Refused |

## The grace-period rule

The clock starts from the rent due date recorded on the rental. The day after that date is day 1 of the grace period, and day 30 is its last day. If the year's rent has been paid by the close of day 30, no late fee arises. If it is still unpaid once day 30 has ended, two things follow together: the late fee for the box size is charged, and the rental moves from active to past due. Paying on day 30 itself is therefore within the grace period.

The grace period is judged on the bank's record of the rent due date and of what has been paid, not on the lessee's recollection.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical rent due date of 1 March):**

| What happens | Result |
|---|---|
| Rent paid on 31 March, the thirtieth grace day | Paid within grace; no late fee; the rental stays active |
| Rent still unpaid when 31 March ends | Late fee charged, dated 1 April, and the rental becomes past due |
| Rent paid on 2 March | Paid within grace; no late fee |

## One fee per rental year

A single late fee is charged for a given rental year, no matter how long that year's rent then remains unpaid. A second year left unpaid would carry its own fee.

## Status and the vault

For every size, a rental that is past due, or that has gone further and is drill pending, is refused access to the vault. Once everything owed on the rental has been paid, a past due rental returns to active.

## Late fees that are later removed

A late fee is not always final. One levied against these terms, or one the bank decides to waive as a courtesy while the customer's courtesy waivers over the most recent 365 days still number fewer than the courtesy allowance, is taken off the rental by means of a credit.
